content: A disaccharide is a type of carbohydrate that consists of two monosaccharide units chemically bonded together. It is one of the four main classifications of carbohydrates, alongside monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, and polysaccharides. Disaccharides are formed through a chemical process known as a dehydration reaction, also referred to as a condensation reaction or dehydration synthesis. During this process, two monosaccharides are joined together, and a molecule of water is removed. For example, lactose, commonly known as milk sugar, is composed of glucose and galactose, while sucrose, or cane sugar, is made up of glucose and fructose. The bond that forms between the two monosaccharides is called a glycosidic bond. The glycosidic bond in disaccharides can form between any hydroxyl group on the monosaccharide components. Variations in the position of the bond (referred to as regiochemistry) and the spatial arrangement of atoms around the bond (stereochemistry, such as alphaor betaconfigurations) result in disaccharides that are diastereoisomers. These isomers exhibit distinct chemical and physical properties. Depending on the specific monosaccharides involved, disaccharides can exhibit a range of characteristics. Some are crystalline, some are water-soluble, and others may have a sweet taste or a sticky texture. Common disaccharides include maltose and cellobiose, which are hydrolysis products of the polysaccharides starch and cellulose, respectively. Less common disaccharides include: Gentiobiose: Composed of two glucose units linked by a β(1→6) bond. Isomaltose: Composed of two glucose units linked by an α(1→6) bond. Kojibiose: Composed of two glucose units linked by an α(1→2) bond. Laminaribiose: Composed of two glucose units linked by a β(1→3) bond. Mannobiose: Composed of two mannose units linked by α(1→2), α(1→3), α(1→4), or α(1→6) bonds. Melibiose: Composed of one glucose unit and one galactose unit linked by an α(1→6) bond. Nigerose: Composed of two glucose units linked by an α(1→3) bond. Rutinose: Composed of one rhamnose unit and one glucose unit linked by an α(1→6) bond. Xylobiose: Composed of two xylopyranose units linked by a β(1→4) bond.
